research_concepts: lineup coverage of organizer, shaper and terminal structural roles
within-team variation in role coverage across lineups
separability of role coverage from player talent and roster counts
talent control in lineup-level influence measures
methodological_questions: Can lineup role coverage be separated from talent and player-count confounds in play-by-play data?
Does talent control behave as intended when talent is measured from the same season's outcomes?
Are role labels derived from the same possession outcomes used to evaluate lineups, creating circularity?
Do placebo or shuffled role assignments produce the same association as the real labels?
Is the number of independent units (team-seasons versus lineup stints) adequate for the within-team contrast?

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality versus talent as predictor of series wins. Talent (RS net-rating) was correlated with adaptation (corr +0.124). After talent control, adaptation was not significant (per-series logistic adapt_diff_z p=0.2755; team-in-series cluster adapt p=0.2449; talent p=0.0095). Recorded failure: n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

Absence validation: real player absences moved the association structure (V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) +0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187] confirmed). The predicted-magnitude tests (V2a rho=+0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667]; V2b rho=+0.253, p=0.115) failed.

Structural concentration versus defensive vulnerability across 30 franchises (n=117). C1a rho=+0.079, p=0.0882, CI [-0.114, +0.234]; C1b rho=+0.095, p=0.0738; robust 0.2/0.3 also failed. Recorded as an adequately powered null, though the CI spans zero.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type, built on reconstructed lineups from the same NBA play-by-play possession dataset. Reported lineup-cell PPP gaps (e.g., Jokic vs MIN 0.814, n=59; Giannis forced PULL_UP 0.848 vs DRIVE) were descriptive, with no placebo or matching, and later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using a team-level talent measure to isolate a coaching or structural adaptation effect on outcomes.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable: after talent control the adaptation effect was not distinguishable (p=0.275), and the sample (n~55 series) could not separate adaptation from roster quality.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of structural change under simulated absences (V2a and V2b).
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable and failing: the magnitude predictions had wide CIs spanning zero (rho=+0.288 with CI [-0.244, +0.667]; rho=+0.253 with CI [-0.262, +0.615]), limited by small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing structural concentration as a predictor of defensive vulnerability.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a powered null with rho near +0.08 to +0.10 and CIs spanning zero across 30 franchises; the recorded limitation includes low power for a large minimum detectable effect.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing lineup and forced-play-type gaps to star suppression without controls.
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching was run; the record notes later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts, so the mechanism stayed unclear.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project studies on this data family repeatedly found that structural or talent-adjacent associations with outcomes are sensitive to talent control and to small sample sizes (FAM:SF-APPS-027, FAM:SF-PAP-024).
Absence-based structural shifts were detectable in one earlier study (FAM:SF20, V1), which suggests that within-team roster changes can move structure, though the magnitude prediction failed.
Lineup-level descriptive gaps built from reconstructed lineups in this dataset were not, by themselves, evidence of an effect (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
evidence_does_not_establish: No returned record tests lineup role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) directly. None of the four records measures it, so whether coverage varies within team or is separable from talent is unknown from this history.
No returned record establishes that talent control behaves correctly when role labels and outcomes come from the same play-by-play data.
No record gives the variance decomposition, the number of within-team lineup contrasts, or any power estimate for coverage effects in these data.
The retrieval does not show whether the role taxonomy is defined, validated, or stable across 2022-23 to 2025-26.
own_inferences: The question is adjacent to the prior failures: talent is confounded with structure (as in SF-APPS-027), sample sizes at the team-season level are small (90 units, 30 franchises), and lineup-level play-by-play gaps are prone to artifacts (as in SF-CHT-009).

Within-team lineup variation is the most promising handle, because it lets team-season talent be held fixed. Possessions are not independent units, so inference must cluster at the team-season or lineup level.
Separability from player counts is plausible to test directly, since coverage likely rises with the number of rotation players on the floor. A count-matched design would be needed.
Using team net rating or lineup net rating from the same season as talent control would create leakage if the role labels are also derived from those possessions.
uncertainties: The exact definitions of organizer, shaper and terminal, and whether they are fixed before outcomes, are not stated in the task or the retrieved records.
Whether the 420,993 possessions across 90 team-seasons provide enough within-team lineup contrasts with sufficient minutes is unknown.
Whether talent can be measured out-of-sample (e.g., prior season, or leave-lineup-out) is not specified.

The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13, and the 2025-26 playoffs only from 2026-06-21. The question date is 2026-07-13, so both are complete, but any partial pulls would need to be excluded.
Retrieval returned records only for adjacent questions; no record on this exact question was retrieved, so prior-work coverage may be incomplete.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not answer the question but show recurring failure modes: talent confounding (SF-APPS-027), underpowered team-level samples (SF-PAP-024, SF20), and descriptive lineup gaps treated as effects without placebo controls (SF-CHT-009). These pushed the decision from a straightforward test toward a proceed-with-changes design that fixes role definitions before outcomes, measures talent out-of-sample, adds placebo role assignments, and reports power before any inferential claim.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels (organizer, shaper, terminal) may be derived from the same possession outcomes used to evaluate lineups; this must be prevented by fixing the mapping before outcome analysis.
Talent and player-count confounds may absorb the coverage effect, as in FAM:SF-APPS-027; talent must be measured out-of-lineup and count-matched.
90 team-seasons and 30 franchises (FAM:SF-PAP-024) give limited between-team power; within-team lineup contrasts must carry the test, and power must be estimated by simulation.
Same-season team or lineup net rating used as talent control leaks outcome information into the control.

prior_work.summary: No returned record tests lineup coverage of organizer, shaper or terminal roles. The four cited records are adjacent: talent-adjusted adaptation (untestable, SF-APPS-027), absence-based structural validation (untestable for magnitude, SF20), structural concentration versus defensive vulnerability (rejected, SF-PAP-024), and descriptive star-lineup suppression gaps with no placebo (not a hypothesis test, SF-CHT-009). They inform risks and design but do not answer the question.

risks.text: Role labels built from the same possessions and points used to evaluate lineups make coverage and outcome partly the same quantity.
Coverage correlates with talent and with the number of players on the floor; without count-matching and out-of-sample talent, separability cannot be claimed (cf. SF-APPS-027).
Using same-season net rating as talent control, or role labels computed from the full season, leaks future or outcome information.
Between-team sample is 90 team-seasons; effect sizes of the order seen in SF-PAP-024 would be undetectable at team level.
Descriptive lineup gaps (SF-CHT-009) can arise from play-type and lineup selection; a placebo role assignment is needed to show the association is specific to the roles.
Role coverage per lineup depends on play-type classification from play-by-play; classification noise may attenuate or inflate coverage.
Some lineups with a given role combination will have few possessions, making lineup-level coverage estimates unstable.
Many role definitions, play types and season splits invite selective reporting unless one primary test is pre-specified.
Play-style and rule changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can shift role frequencies over time, so pooling seasons may mix regimes.

design.estimand: Within-team-season association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper or terminal on the floor) and lineup possession-level points per possession, after conditioning on out-of-lineup talent and on the number of rotation players, with the coverage effect reported as separable from talent and count (partial contribution).
design.unit: Lineup stint (lineup of five within a team-season), with inference clustered by team-season; possessions aggregated within stints.
design.sample: Derivation: NBA 2022-23 and 2023-24 regular seasons, used to fix role definitions and talent measure. Confirmation: NBA 2024-25 regular season and 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs (2022-23 to 2025-26; 2025-26 complete from 2026-06-21) used only as an out-of-sample validation of the confirmed rule. Exclude any partial pulls.
design.power: Estimated by simulation before analysis: simulate stints with the observed count of within-team lineup contrasts and cluster structure; require 80% power at a pre-specified minimum effect (set before analysis, e.g., a PPP difference equal to a fixed fraction of the coverage-to-PPP gap). If power is below 80%, report the question as uncertain rather than null.
design.controls: Talent from out-of-lineup minutes (leave-lineup-out or prior-season team net rating, never same-stint or same-season outcomes); number of rotation players on the floor (count-matched or fixed effects); minutes; opponent strength; lineup-level shot quality where available. Role labels fixed from the derivation seasons before any outcome comparison.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo role labels with the same frequency distribution but randomised across players; (2) shuffled coverage within team-season; (3) a null-control outcome that should not depend on roles (e.g., free-throw rate); (4) out-of-sample check on playoffs. The hypothesis fails if the real coverage effect is not larger than placebo distributions or if the talent-adjusted effect has a CI spanning zero.
design.multiplicity: One primary test: the talent- and count-adjusted coverage coefficient. Role definitions, play-type mappings and season splits are fixed in advance; secondary analyses labelled exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) the primary coefficient's cluster-bootstrap 95% CI excludes zero, (b) it exceeds the 95th percentile of the placebo distribution, (c) talent and count controls do not absorb it (partial effect retained), and (d) it replicates in the 2024-25 and 2025-26 regular-season confirmation sample. Rejected only if powered (per the simulation) and the CI excludes a pre-specified minimum effect. Otherwise report uncertain or untestable.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs as listed; 2025-26 regular season used only from its complete version (2026-04-13 onward); 2025-26 playoffs only from complete version (2026-06-21 onward); play-by-play, rotation intervals, starters, and derived play-type possession records, with the version and extraction date recorded in the pre-registration.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
